summary: Madison County lookout built in 1943 by conscientious objectors and removed in 1959; the mountain is now a park hiking destination.

facts.status_note: Lookout removed in 1959 according to one source; the summit is reached on park trails.

access.note: Hikers reach the summit on park trails. One source says a ticket is required to hike Old Rag for most of the year.

visit.trail_note: The most common route starts at a parking area in Nethers; a circuit hike covers 9 miles (14.5 km).

events.note: Built by conscientious objectors working for the CPS program, who hand-carried materials up a steep grade
Photo caption shows a ranger beside the tower operating a fire finder
Date given on the Old Rag page; a park-wide page dates dismantling of its towers to the early 1960s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Old Rag page gives 1959 for removal. The park-wide page says dismantling of its towers began in the early 1960s. The story uses the 1959 date from the Old Rag page.

notes_for_editor: Structure type disagrees: the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Ground, while the 1957 Willhite caption calls it the Old Rag Fire Tower. The story reports both. The 1943 build and 1950 staffing appear in two Shenandoah National Park Facebook posts, but only in search snippets, so they are not cited. The ticket rule is one Willhite statement and may be out of date; check current park rules before publishing. Willhite's Old Rag page gives the loop as 9.8 miles; the story uses Wikipedia's 9-mile circuit figure and attributes it to Wikipedia. The 1959 removal date conflicts with the early-1960s dismantling date on the park-wide page, and the story says so. No photo licence was checked, so no photos are added.
